keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-file: a .pk8 to put in --offer-slot in place of the snapshot's record: stored or party form, encrypted or PKHeX's decrypted export. Its OT name and ids become the snapshot's unless --offer-file-as-is. Repeatable, one per trade on the session: the console's player picks again from the box; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-raid-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-raid-join:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for every offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-file-as-is: keep the file's own OT name and trainer ids
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-species: build the record in --offer-slot instead of sending it as it came: this national dex number, in the party record the snapshot advertises AND in the offer, so the two still tell one story
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-ability: the ability id of the built record; --offer-species leaves the template's ability where it was
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-level: the level byte at 0x148 of the built record, 1..100; the experience word is left alone unless --offer-experience is given
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-experience: the experience word at 0x10 of the built record
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-moves: four move ids, comma-separated; 0 empties a slot. PP is left as the template had it
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-nickname: the nickname of the built record; sets the nicknamed flag
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-ot: the original trainer name of the built record
keys.swsh-raid-join:--offer-ivs: six IVs, comma-separated, in PKHeX's HP,ATK,DEF,SPE,SPA,SPD order
keys.swsh-raid-join:--save-offer: write the PK8 we will offer to this file, before the radio is touched
keys.swsh-raid-join:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-raid-join:--save-offered: write the PK8 the console traded to this file, once the trade completes; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-raid-join:--rpc-clock-delta: how far to advance a trade RPC's clock in our answer. 5 is nxldn-lab's and is the one number in this path nothing here has measured
keys.swsh-raid-join:--rpc-pair-advance: after answering an RPC pair, send BOTH members again with the clock advanced by this much. The console advances its own pair's clock by 2 each burst (b41c, b61c, b81c). A repeated clock is a repeated state, so an answer that carries one clock never moves ours. 0 is off
keys.swsh-raid-join:--selection-start: send our own 40050 pair the moment the console says id 130 pingSynced, before its own selection burst. nxldn-lab's client opens the selection phase this way and nothing here has ever opened one; the console sends 820000001a00 in our own captures 0.3 s before its 40050 burst
keys.swsh-raid-join:--ack-snapshot: ACK the console's 0x84 fragments (kind 0x21, a contiguous base and a bitmask). Nothing here has ever acked this protocol, which is why the console retransmits one snapshot 19142 times and never moves on
keys.swsh-raid-join:--send-snapshot: a 3456-byte trade snapshot to send back on 0x84 once the console sends its own, or live (the default under --preset trade) for the console's own from this session. A short 2965-byte payload is inflated first. The identity is rewritten by --snapshot-name/-tid/-sid
keys.swsh-raid-join:--snapshot-port: Pia port(s) for our 0x84 messages; the console sends on 0
keys.swsh-raid-join:--snapshot-repeat: between whole re-sends; the console retransmits its own until acked
keys.swsh-raid-join:--sync-answers: answer with `pokeldn.swsh.trade.SYNC_ANSWERS` instead of echoing one payload: the ping, and the three other sync holders the console is expected to raise after the trade snapshot. A payload with no rule is REPORTED and left unanswered - that report is the point of the run
keys.swsh-raid-join:--send-mirror: send back whatever the console last said on this protocol, rather than the fixed --send-data. --send-data is still the first payload, before the console has said anything
keys.swsh-raid-join:--send-count: how many sequence ids of ours to send in all; 0 has no limit. One message does not hold the console's state; it sends its own heartbeat about 580 times in 180 s
keys.swsh-raid-join:--send-period: the retransmit interval. A window retransmits until it is acked
keys.swsh-raid-join:--send-seconds: how long to keep retransmitting if nothing acknowledges it; 0 sends until the run ends
keys.swsh-raid-join:--raid-join: a Max Raid den guest: after the snapshot send PlayerInfo, BattleReady and SelectPokemon (the --offer-slot Pokemon); use with --scene 60006
keys.swsh-raid-join:--lair-join: a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) guest: the lobby, the paths and the battles; use with --scene 50000
keys.swsh-raid-join:--lair-rental: an encrypted party PK8 sent as our rental instead of the offered one
keys.swsh-raid-join:--lair-rental-choice: the offer place we take; by default the first the host left
keys.swsh-raid-join:--raid-ready: press ready this many seconds after the host acked the lobby messages
keys.swsh-raid-join:--raid-move: the move slot our Pokemon uses every turn
keys.swsh-raid-join:--raid-name: the name the raid lobby shows for us
keys.swsh-raid-join:--hold-after-trade: leave the seat this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-raid-join:--grace: seconds past --hold to keep a session whose trade is under way: the console has offered and the ladder has not finished
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--ip-host: host an emulated console over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio and no root
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--our-ip: with --ip-host or --lan, the address to advertise; --lan without it takes the address on the subnet the console browses from
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lan: host a session for a console in Sword's LAN mode on this IP network (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no root, no keys
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lan-max-players: --lan: the maximum the session info states
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lan-broadcast: --lan: the subnet broadcast address the console's challenge uses
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lan-console-ip: --lan from a loopback address: the address a console on this machine believes it has; default this machine's own
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--advert: optional Sword advertisement (hex, raw, or swsh_net_facts.json); without one, build a fresh station record
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--snapshot: optional saved Sword 0x84 snapshot; otherwise use the joining console's snapshot from this session
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--offer-file: a PK8 to place in the offered party slot, encrypted or PKHeX export. Repeatable, one per trade: the player trades again from the box, or searches again; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for the offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--card-set: set a field of the League Card the console may keep after the trade (pokeldn.swsh.league_card: name, trainer_id, dex_owned, poke1_species, ...)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--end-delay: with --migrate, ladder done to box command 3 and the migration
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--migrate: end with box command 3 and MIGRATION_START, as the retail Sword that led our joiner did; by default the host keeps the session
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--accept-first: accept without waiting for the joiner's acceptance, as a player would; for our own joiner, which accepts after its partner
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lead: test only, for bin/swsh_connect.py: act as a console host's player: after a trade with another --offer-file queued, offer it from the box this many seconds after the ladder, without waiting for the joiner's offer
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--received: write the joiner's Pokemon here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--code: the Link Code the player searches with, e.g. 12345678; none by default
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--network-id: advertise 0x00, hex; a searching Sword joins only a larger one than its own; default 0xFFFF and two random bytes
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--hold-after-trade: close the session this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-boss: host a Max Raid den lobby with this boss instead of a Link Trade (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-reward: a reward row, item id and count; up to 15; none gives an emulated den's rows
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-seed: the BattleSeed value; random by default
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-ready: our player readies this long after the guest's lobby opens
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-event: host a Max Raid with a boss of this Wild Area Event delivery (an EventsGallery 'Index NNN' folder) instead of --raid-boss; its rewards unless --raid-reward (docs/swsh_raid.md, Event raids)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-event-boss: with --raid-event: the boss, numbered as the list printed without it
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-version: with --raid-event: whose table the boss comes from; the advertisement's version by default
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-area: with --raid-event: the den area whose table the boss comes from
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-event-drops: with --raid-event: roll each drop's chance as a den does, or give every drop
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-gigantamax: the --raid-boss boss is Gigantamax; a retail console accepts it where a base den holds that Gigantamax Pokemon (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-boss-as-is: send the --raid-boss file's own level, IVs, nature, size and PID instead of a den seed's; a console's catch then fails PKHeX's raid check (docs/swsh_raid.md, A boss a catch keeps legal)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--raid-console-serve: put the console first in BattleStart and framework object 0, so it serves the battle and the board answers as a client (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lair-legendary: host a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) lobby whose legendary is this species; the host leaves once the adventure starts (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lair-scene: the lobby's LDN scene; by default the console's own lobby's, found by a scan, else 50000 (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lair-seed: the adventure seed (ChikaBattleSeed): the rentals and encounters; random by default
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--lair-leave: leave this long after the legendary is sent; a computer partner then takes our seat and picks our rental
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
keys.swsh-lair-raid-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--preset: the tested flag set: 'capture' records the console's party snapshot, 'trade' needs --send-snapshot, 'raid' a Max Raid den guest, 'lair' a Dynamax Adventure guest
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ip-join: join an emulated console hosting over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio, no root, no keys. Each of --scans waits --dwell seconds for an answer
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--our-ip: --ip-join: our own address on that LAN
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--scan-ip: --ip-join: the address a scan leaves from; default --our-ip
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lan: join a console in Sword's LAN mode over the IP network: its address, the subnet broadcast, or auto for every local /24 (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no keys
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lan-max-players: --lan: the session maximum to browse for; default 4 for a raid or adventure, 2 for a trade
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lan-host-wait: --lan: seconds to repeat the host request before the station handshake
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lan-quiet: --lan: seconds of silence that mean the console left
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--scans: scans for a matching search (--scene) before giving up
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--scene: the LDN scene id to seat in: 60001 a Link Trade search; any takes the first Sword network (a Max Raid den, docs/swsh_gift.md)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--listen-first: seconds of listening before the first packet out, so the capture holds the console's own rate to compare against
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--station-sweep: readings of the header byte at 0x05, in order; the IV's source id follows each one
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--quiet-for: seconds without an update session that count as the rebroadcast stopping - the console sends ten a second, so this is fifteen missed
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--seq-delta: THE CONTROL. Ack a sequence id the console never sent: a rebroadcast that carries on under --seq-delta 1 is what attributes a stop under 0 to the ack's CONTENT rather than to our merely having transmitted
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--connect: after the ack, sweep the version-4 connection request on protocol 0x14
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--nat-flags: values for byte [1], list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--request-gap: seconds between requests; the console answered BDSP's in 40 ms
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--connect-station: values for the header byte at 0x05 on the requests, and their IV source id; list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--respond: answer a connection request the CONSOLE sends us with a connection response
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--respond-with: whose constant and variable id go in the response's two id fields - a deduction, so 'both' alternates them across the retransmits
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--request-platform: values for the platform byte at [2]. 9 is the real one; ANY other value is answered with a connection response rather than dropped, which is the probe for whether our message reaches the 0x14 handler at all
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--request-flags: values for the MESSAGE flags byte. 0x09 is what the console puts on its own Local Protocol messages; BDSP's station requests carry 0x11
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--request-unicast: send the requests to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--request-broadcast: send them to the broadcast address instead
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--src-var: our own station variable id; fresh random when omitted, because a reused one is 'already one of my stations' on BDSP
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--no-variable-id: clear [3], which makes the console skip the variable-id comparison
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--unicast: send to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join: after the station handshake closes, send the Mesh Protocol (0x18) join request and ack whatever comes back
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-wait: how long to wait for the station acceptance before giving up on joining
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-seconds: how long to retransmit the join request; Pia's own joiner gives up at 10
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-gap: Pia retransmits an unacknowledged join request every 500 ms
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-port: the Pia port the join travels on; the update mesh uses the reliable one
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-station-index: byte [1]. 0xFD is what 0x017c1700 compares against; anything else is the instrument that says the handler was reached
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--join-ack-id: fixed ack id for the join request; random when omitted
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--answer-rtt: answer the console's 0x58 RTT requests. Sixteen bytes at version 4, and the reply echoes the seven bytes nothing has read yet
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ack-reliable: acknowledge the 0x7C reliable window. The pass signal is the retransmits STOPPING and the sequence ids moving on
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ack-slots: which of the 32 ack slots to fill; "all" (the default) fills every one, because only the slot at some station index is read and whose index it is has not been settled. "0" is the console, "1" is us
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ack-lowest-pending: the header's own 'lowest sequence pending ack'. We have sent nothing on this protocol, so 1 (the next id we would use) and 0 are both readings; the console itself sends 1 while waiting on its own first message
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--data-destination: the station BITMAP on 0x58 and 0x7C. The console sends 2 to us, station index 1; 1 is the bit for station 0, which is the console
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-data: send APPLICATION DATA once the mesh is up - the first of the project. The payload as hex; "610000000a00" is the six bytes the console repeats at us on 0x7C. Nothing is sent without this flag
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-protocol: 0x80 (the broadcast reliable window, the default: it asks us for sequence 1 once a second) or 0x7c (the unicast one, which has never had an ack to send us because it has never had our data)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-sequence: the sequence id. 1 is what both windows ask for; the first message also carries FLAG_IS_INITIALIZED and DEFINES where the stream starts
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-stream: the stream id. 0 is what the console sends on both protocols
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-destinations: the header's destination list. "console" names its station constant id, which is what its own broadcast acks do to us; "none" sends count 0, which 0x01859578 never filters and every 0x7C message carries. "auto" mirrors the console per protocol: none on 0x7C, the console on 0x80
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-zlib: compress the message, the way the console compresses every 0x80 message it sends. The flag is the Pia message's (0x10 at version 4), so this is free either way - and it is one variable, so sweep it alone
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-port: the Pia message port. The console sends its 0x80 acks on 0 AND 1, each packet carrying both; "0,1" mirrors that
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-wait: how long to wait for the station handshake before giving up on sending
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-after: seconds after acceptance before the first data message, so the mesh join and the RTT exchange are already running when it lands
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send2-data: a SECOND stream, on --send2-protocol, sent once the console says --send2-trigger. `60ea000012020801` is BlockDataHolder{imReady:true}, which the console says on 0x80 and waits on
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send2-trigger: wait for this payload on --send2-protocol before sending; omit to send as soon as the mesh is up
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--trade-ready: after our offer is acknowledged, send imReady on the TRADE holder (20030). The console has never sent these bytes and the published client waits for them before it offers, so it may be our turn to say them
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--rpc-port-answers: answer the trade RPC on its OWN Pia port with its own reliable window. The console sends them on 0x7C port 1; an answer on port 0 lands on a window it does not read them on
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--answer-migration: answer the console's MIGRATION_START on 0x18 port 1 with a MIGRATION_RESPONSE. `440001` arrives there only when the player accepts, and the console goes silent on every window afterwards: the last thing it asks for is two bytes of mesh, not application data
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--leave-with-host: when the hosting console leaves, ack its update session carrying the host-migration state and leave the network on its START_HOST_MIGRATION, as its own clients do; each step waits 10 s unanswered
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--migration-answer: what to send when the console migrates the mesh. "auto" sends MIGRATION_FINISH when the start names US as the next host and a MIGRATION_RESPONSE when it names anyone else, which is what the binary says. "response" always answers 0x48, for comparison
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--open-content: after our offer is acknowledged, send `ping` on content N's 10000-base holder for each N - `382700000a00` for 40, which is exactly the opener nxldn-lab's client sends to start the confirmation phase, rebuilt here from our own content registry rather than copied
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--confirm-command: when the CONFIRMATION envelope (40040) sends a four-byte status whose body ends `0100` - the same cue the selection content sends before its Pokemon - reply with SyncSaveDataHolder{syncCommand{data:N}} on that content's 10000-base holder, id 10040, reliable port 0, and answer the status itself on port 1. Content 40 takes a command and not a Pokemon: its parser 0x010df6d0 accepts one submessage carrying one int32. Its own machine sends 0, 1, 2 and 3 in that order (swsh_trade.SYNC_COMMANDS)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--confirm-phase: answer the confirmation content's four-byte steps with phase N in the LOW u16 instead of echoing the console's own. The console reads its phase out of exactly those bytes (`0x006d6490` stores them, `0x006d3260` reads them), and every step this project has sent so far echoed the value back unchanged
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ladder-refresh: while the confirmation ladder waits on the console, send our 40040 pair again every SECONDS with its clock advanced to the present. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--abort-on-stall: once the confirmation ladder has produced its first step, end the run as soon as SECONDS pass with no NEW step body: stop transmitting, drop the link and let the console report a lost connection. Holding a stalled ladder open with acks instead makes the game declare the TRADE failed, which costs the player about an hour. Nothing but acks follows the last step body. 0 is off and the hold runs in full.
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--confirm-commands: the handshake form of --confirm-command: send the NEXT of these on each new four-byte body the confirmation content puts on elementId 20000. Content 40's own machine sends 0,1,2,3 and parks after each; one command buys two rungs and then the ladder stops
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--confirm-final-delt: after the CONFIRMATION content answers our syncCommand with a hash, re-arm the 40040 pair and send BOTH members again at this clock delta - the move --selection-final-delta makes on 40050, which carries the selection phase past its own hash
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-final-de: after the selection HASH is answered, send the 40050 pair AGAIN - both members - at this clock delta. nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta` is 9 (nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta`). --rpc-pair latches per envelope, so the second pair needs the latch cleared. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--open-content-offer: make --open-content send our PK8 on the 10000-base holder instead of an empty `ping`. The ping opens content 50 and is taken as our Pokemon: the console reaches the confirmation phase and asks the player to trade theirs for an egg. Same moment, same holder, a Pokemon in it
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--box-on-accept: send these box commands the moment MIGRATION_START arrives - the only signal that says the player pressed accept. The console keeps acking for about five seconds after it
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--box-period: seconds between the queued post-offer payloads. Spread them so the sweep spans the accept: the console tears down on the accept, not on a timer, so commands sent inside a couple of seconds all land before it
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-offer: when the console follows its selection-phase Pokemon with the status whose body ends `0100`, offer OUR Pokemon on that content's 10000-base holder (id 10050) on reliable port 0 and answer the status on port 1
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--pair-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, open content N's phase by sending the two-member RPC pair for it (40 is the confirmation). A pair is the only shape that opens a phase on this console: 40030 opened the offer and 40050 the selection. A bare content ping (`382700000a00`) and a bare sync-120 ping (`780000000a00`) are both ignored
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--sync-after-offer: queue a sync on holder N right behind our selection offer, in the branch that actually runs when --selection-offer is on. --sync-after-hash cannot fire there: this one can
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--sync-field: which SyncPingDataHolder field --sync-after-hash sends: 1 ping, 2 pingReply, 3 pingSynced (`780000001a00`, the one the trace records)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--sync-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, send `ping` on sync holder N (120 is the confirmation's) on port 0. The console drives 97, 60000, 110 and 130 itself and opens the selection phase when 130's pingSynced lands; it never sends 120. A phase follows its sync, not a content ping
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--open-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, `ping` content N's 10000-base holder on port 0 to open the next phase - 40 is the confirmation, so this sends `382700000a00`. The console stops sending 40050 once the hash answer lands and says nothing further; Pia retransmits anything it still waits on, so that silence means satisfied and the next phase needs opening
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--rpc-bodies: answer every DISTINCT (envelope, base, field-5 body) in the 40000 band once, on top of the opening pair. The clock advances on every message so the payload cannot be the key, but the body can: `00000000` and `000018fc` are the openers and anything else is new. A per-envelope guard stops answering at the hash body and stalls there
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--rpc-pair: answer the console's 40030 RPC as the PAIR it is: collect both members one per base, 10000 then 20000, keyed on the BASE FIELD. `payload[5] in (0x19, 0x1A)` is the inner length and moves with the sender's station-id varint (0x1A/0x1B on some consoles). Send both once in that order and nothing more on this window; `said_by_port` keeps only the last payload, so a mirror sends one member repeatedly and never the other
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--open-early: `ping` content N's 10000-base holder at the 0x84 snapshot ack, before either side offers. The console's box send is gated on a ready bool at content+0x4c that only `0x010ce040` sets, on a zero result code; until then every command the game tries to send is parked in content+0x48. A parked command that does not match the next one sets the error byte +0x4d, and `0x010c9bb0` turns that into trade state 9: abort, with nothing on the application layer
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--box-open: send these box commands as soon as the console acks our 0x84 snapshot - BEFORE either side offers a Pokemon. The game sends command 3 exactly once, on the first frame after its trade session is built and only when the role bit at session+0x419 is clear (0x010c9bb0), so one of the two sides owes the other an opener before anything else happens. Sent after both offers instead, the console leaves while the player is still picking
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--box-commands: after our offer is acknowledged, send boxSyncStateCommand{data:N} on the trade holder for each N in turn, one per acknowledged sequence. 20030 is a BoxSyncStateDataHolder and its field 2 is a command enum; this project 1 offers and 2 withdraws; 4 confirms and 5 withdraws the confirmation
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--snapshot-account: replace the three ids at the front of the snapshot's profile (pseudo device id, account Uid, network service account id). They are the console's own, handed back unchanged otherwise
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-offer-da: with --selection-offer, answer the console's selection status with our PK8 in field 5 (`body`) of a 40050 Data carrying OUR ownerId, on the RPC port, instead of a PokemonTradeDataHolder on 10050 port 0. Content 50's receive handler resolves the sender to a station index and drops silently when it cannot; the holder shape carries no owner
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-offer-sw: send our PK8 as a Data on elementId 10000 and as a holder on the 30000-base id (30050), which every content registers. More than one variable at once
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-offer-hi: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 as a PokemonTradeDataHolder on the 20000-base holder (id 20050), which is where the BOX phase's own Pokemon rides one content over. Overrides --selection-offer-mirror and --selection-offer-data
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-offer-mi: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 in a 40050 carrying the console's OWN field set - syncId, clock, body, and neither elementId nor ownerId, which is how its own selection offer decodes. Overrides --selection-offer-data
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-echo: offer back the exact PK8 the console just offered us, unchanged, instead of one out of --send-snapshot. These bytes came out of its own save, so a run that still aborts rules the record out
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-on-50: put our PK8 in field 5 of the 40050 pair's second member. Content 50 is PokemonTradeDataHolder, the transfer; content 30 is the box exchange. A 344-byte PK8 rides that field
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-selection: WHEN to open the selection phase with a 40050 pair on 0x7c port 1. "offer" sends it as soon as our offer is acknowledged, the only window the console is still reading in; "migration" sends it on the migration start, after the console has stopped. The pair is the same envelope as the console's own 40030 at offset 50 with our station id; the builder reproduces its 40030 pair byte for byte
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--update-mesh: once the migration makes us the host, broadcast UPDATE_MESH the way the console did: its own last one with the host index set to ours. The console stops sending these once it hands the role over, and the mesh is gone about 1.3 s later if nothing takes over
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--update-mesh-period: how often to broadcast it; the console sent one about every 2 s
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--migration-period: how often to retransmit the migration response until it is acked
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--answer-once: answer each payload the console sends ONCE instead of re-deriving an answer to its last payload every period. `said` never clears, so without this an offer goes out hundreds of times. The console sends each of its own messages once
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-slot: which party slot of --send-snapshot to offer back, 1-6; 0 offers nothing and only records what the console offers us
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-file: a .pk8 to put in --offer-slot in place of the snapshot's record: stored or party form, encrypted or PKHeX's decrypted export. Its OT name and ids become the snapshot's unless --offer-file-as-is. Repeatable, one per trade on the session: the console's player picks again from the box; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for every offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-file-as-is: keep the file's own OT name and trainer ids
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-species: build the record in --offer-slot instead of sending it as it came: this national dex number, in the party record the snapshot advertises AND in the offer, so the two still tell one story
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-ability: the ability id of the built record; --offer-species leaves the template's ability where it was
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-level: the level byte at 0x148 of the built record, 1..100; the experience word is left alone unless --offer-experience is given
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-experience: the experience word at 0x10 of the built record
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-moves: four move ids, comma-separated; 0 empties a slot. PP is left as the template had it
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-nickname: the nickname of the built record; sets the nicknamed flag
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-ot: the original trainer name of the built record
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--offer-ivs: six IVs, comma-separated, in PKHeX's HP,ATK,DEF,SPE,SPA,SPD order
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--save-offer: write the PK8 we will offer to this file, before the radio is touched
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--save-offered: write the PK8 the console traded to this file, once the trade completes; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--rpc-clock-delta: how far to advance a trade RPC's clock in our answer. 5 is nxldn-lab's and is the one number in this path nothing here has measured
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--rpc-pair-advance: after answering an RPC pair, send BOTH members again with the clock advanced by this much. The console advances its own pair's clock by 2 each burst (b41c, b61c, b81c). A repeated clock is a repeated state, so an answer that carries one clock never moves ours. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--selection-start: send our own 40050 pair the moment the console says id 130 pingSynced, before its own selection burst. nxldn-lab's client opens the selection phase this way and nothing here has ever opened one; the console sends 820000001a00 in our own captures 0.3 s before its 40050 burst
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--ack-snapshot: ACK the console's 0x84 fragments (kind 0x21, a contiguous base and a bitmask). Nothing here has ever acked this protocol, which is why the console retransmits one snapshot 19142 times and never moves on
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-snapshot: a 3456-byte trade snapshot to send back on 0x84 once the console sends its own, or live (the default under --preset trade) for the console's own from this session. A short 2965-byte payload is inflated first. The identity is rewritten by --snapshot-name/-tid/-sid
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--snapshot-port: Pia port(s) for our 0x84 messages; the console sends on 0
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--snapshot-repeat: between whole re-sends; the console retransmits its own until acked
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--sync-answers: answer with `pokeldn.swsh.trade.SYNC_ANSWERS` instead of echoing one payload: the ping, and the three other sync holders the console is expected to raise after the trade snapshot. A payload with no rule is REPORTED and left unanswered - that report is the point of the run
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-mirror: send back whatever the console last said on this protocol, rather than the fixed --send-data. --send-data is still the first payload, before the console has said anything
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-count: how many sequence ids of ours to send in all; 0 has no limit. One message does not hold the console's state; it sends its own heartbeat about 580 times in 180 s
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-period: the retransmit interval. A window retransmits until it is acked
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--send-seconds: how long to keep retransmitting if nothing acknowledges it; 0 sends until the run ends
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--raid-join: a Max Raid den guest: after the snapshot send PlayerInfo, BattleReady and SelectPokemon (the --offer-slot Pokemon); use with --scene 60006
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lair-join: a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) guest: the lobby, the paths and the battles; use with --scene 50000
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lair-rental: an encrypted party PK8 sent as our rental instead of the offered one
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--lair-rental-choice: the offer place we take; by default the first the host left
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--raid-ready: press ready this many seconds after the host acked the lobby messages
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--raid-move: the move slot our Pokemon uses every turn
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--raid-name: the name the raid lobby shows for us
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--hold-after-trade: leave the seat this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-lair-raid-join:--grace: seconds past --hold to keep a session whose trade is under way: the console has offered and the ladder has not finished
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--ip-host: host an emulated console over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio and no root
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--our-ip: with --ip-host or --lan, the address to advertise; --lan without it takes the address on the subnet the console browses from
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lan: host a session for a console in Sword's LAN mode on this IP network (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no root, no keys
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lan-max-players: --lan: the maximum the session info states
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lan-broadcast: --lan: the subnet broadcast address the console's challenge uses
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lan-console-ip: --lan from a loopback address: the address a console on this machine believes it has; default this machine's own
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--advert: optional Sword advertisement (hex, raw, or swsh_net_facts.json); without one, build a fresh station record
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--snapshot: optional saved Sword 0x84 snapshot; otherwise use the joining console's snapshot from this session
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--offer-file: a PK8 to place in the offered party slot, encrypted or PKHeX export. Repeatable, one per trade: the player trades again from the box, or searches again; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for the offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--card-set: set a field of the League Card the console may keep after the trade (pokeldn.swsh.league_card: name, trainer_id, dex_owned, poke1_species, ...)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--end-delay: with --migrate, ladder done to box command 3 and the migration
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--migrate: end with box command 3 and MIGRATION_START, as the retail Sword that led our joiner did; by default the host keeps the session
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--accept-first: accept without waiting for the joiner's acceptance, as a player would; for our own joiner, which accepts after its partner
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lead: test only, for bin/swsh_connect.py: act as a console host's player: after a trade with another --offer-file queued, offer it from the box this many seconds after the ladder, without waiting for the joiner's offer
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--received: write the joiner's Pokemon here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--code: the Link Code the player searches with, e.g. 12345678; none by default
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--network-id: advertise 0x00, hex; a searching Sword joins only a larger one than its own; default 0xFFFF and two random bytes
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--hold-after-trade: close the session this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-boss: host a Max Raid den lobby with this boss instead of a Link Trade (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-reward: a reward row, item id and count; up to 15; none gives an emulated den's rows
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-seed: the BattleSeed value; random by default
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-ready: our player readies this long after the guest's lobby opens
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-event: host a Max Raid with a boss of this Wild Area Event delivery (an EventsGallery 'Index NNN' folder) instead of --raid-boss; its rewards unless --raid-reward (docs/swsh_raid.md, Event raids)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-event-boss: with --raid-event: the boss, numbered as the list printed without it
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-version: with --raid-event: whose table the boss comes from; the advertisement's version by default
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-area: with --raid-event: the den area whose table the boss comes from
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-event-drops: with --raid-event: roll each drop's chance as a den does, or give every drop
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-gigantamax: the --raid-boss boss is Gigantamax; a retail console accepts it where a base den holds that Gigantamax Pokemon (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-boss-as-is: send the --raid-boss file's own level, IVs, nature, size and PID instead of a den seed's; a console's catch then fails PKHeX's raid check (docs/swsh_raid.md, A boss a catch keeps legal)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--raid-console-serves: put the console first in BattleStart and framework object 0, so it serves the battle and the board answers as a client (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lair-legendary: host a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) lobby whose legendary is this species; the host leaves once the adventure starts (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lair-scene: the lobby's LDN scene; by default the console's own lobby's, found by a scan, else 50000 (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lair-seed: the adventure seed (ChikaBattleSeed): the rentals and encounters; random by default
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--lair-leave: leave this long after the legendary is sent; a computer partner then takes our seat and picks our rental
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
keys.swsh-lan-raid-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--preset: the tested flag set: 'capture' records the console's party snapshot, 'trade' needs --send-snapshot, 'raid' a Max Raid den guest, 'lair' a Dynamax Adventure guest
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ip-join: join an emulated console hosting over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio, no root, no keys. Each of --scans waits --dwell seconds for an answer
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--our-ip: --ip-join: our own address on that LAN
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--scan-ip: --ip-join: the address a scan leaves from; default --our-ip
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lan: join a console in Sword's LAN mode over the IP network: its address, the subnet broadcast, or auto for every local /24 (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no keys
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lan-max-players: --lan: the session maximum to browse for; default 4 for a raid or adventure, 2 for a trade
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lan-host-wait: --lan: seconds to repeat the host request before the station handshake
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lan-quiet: --lan: seconds of silence that mean the console left
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--scans: scans for a matching search (--scene) before giving up
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--scene: the LDN scene id to seat in: 60001 a Link Trade search; any takes the first Sword network (a Max Raid den, docs/swsh_gift.md)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--listen-first: seconds of listening before the first packet out, so the capture holds the console's own rate to compare against
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--station-sweep: readings of the header byte at 0x05, in order; the IV's source id follows each one
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--quiet-for: seconds without an update session that count as the rebroadcast stopping - the console sends ten a second, so this is fifteen missed
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--seq-delta: THE CONTROL. Ack a sequence id the console never sent: a rebroadcast that carries on under --seq-delta 1 is what attributes a stop under 0 to the ack's CONTENT rather than to our merely having transmitted
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--connect: after the ack, sweep the version-4 connection request on protocol 0x14
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--nat-flags: values for byte [1], list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--request-gap: seconds between requests; the console answered BDSP's in 40 ms
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--connect-station: values for the header byte at 0x05 on the requests, and their IV source id; list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--respond: answer a connection request the CONSOLE sends us with a connection response
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--respond-with: whose constant and variable id go in the response's two id fields - a deduction, so 'both' alternates them across the retransmits
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--request-platform: values for the platform byte at [2]. 9 is the real one; ANY other value is answered with a connection response rather than dropped, which is the probe for whether our message reaches the 0x14 handler at all
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--request-flags: values for the MESSAGE flags byte. 0x09 is what the console puts on its own Local Protocol messages; BDSP's station requests carry 0x11
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--request-unicast: send the requests to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--request-broadcast: send them to the broadcast address instead
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--src-var: our own station variable id; fresh random when omitted, because a reused one is 'already one of my stations' on BDSP
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--no-variable-id: clear [3], which makes the console skip the variable-id comparison
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--unicast: send to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join: after the station handshake closes, send the Mesh Protocol (0x18) join request and ack whatever comes back
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-wait: how long to wait for the station acceptance before giving up on joining
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-seconds: how long to retransmit the join request; Pia's own joiner gives up at 10
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-gap: Pia retransmits an unacknowledged join request every 500 ms
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-port: the Pia port the join travels on; the update mesh uses the reliable one
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-station-index: byte [1]. 0xFD is what 0x017c1700 compares against; anything else is the instrument that says the handler was reached
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--join-ack-id: fixed ack id for the join request; random when omitted
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--answer-rtt: answer the console's 0x58 RTT requests. Sixteen bytes at version 4, and the reply echoes the seven bytes nothing has read yet
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ack-reliable: acknowledge the 0x7C reliable window. The pass signal is the retransmits STOPPING and the sequence ids moving on
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ack-slots: which of the 32 ack slots to fill; "all" (the default) fills every one, because only the slot at some station index is read and whose index it is has not been settled. "0" is the console, "1" is us
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ack-lowest-pending: the header's own 'lowest sequence pending ack'. We have sent nothing on this protocol, so 1 (the next id we would use) and 0 are both readings; the console itself sends 1 while waiting on its own first message
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--data-destination: the station BITMAP on 0x58 and 0x7C. The console sends 2 to us, station index 1; 1 is the bit for station 0, which is the console
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-data: send APPLICATION DATA once the mesh is up - the first of the project. The payload as hex; "610000000a00" is the six bytes the console repeats at us on 0x7C. Nothing is sent without this flag
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-protocol: 0x80 (the broadcast reliable window, the default: it asks us for sequence 1 once a second) or 0x7c (the unicast one, which has never had an ack to send us because it has never had our data)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-sequence: the sequence id. 1 is what both windows ask for; the first message also carries FLAG_IS_INITIALIZED and DEFINES where the stream starts
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-stream: the stream id. 0 is what the console sends on both protocols
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-destinations: the header's destination list. "console" names its station constant id, which is what its own broadcast acks do to us; "none" sends count 0, which 0x01859578 never filters and every 0x7C message carries. "auto" mirrors the console per protocol: none on 0x7C, the console on 0x80
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-zlib: compress the message, the way the console compresses every 0x80 message it sends. The flag is the Pia message's (0x10 at version 4), so this is free either way - and it is one variable, so sweep it alone
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-port: the Pia message port. The console sends its 0x80 acks on 0 AND 1, each packet carrying both; "0,1" mirrors that
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-wait: how long to wait for the station handshake before giving up on sending
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-after: seconds after acceptance before the first data message, so the mesh join and the RTT exchange are already running when it lands
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send2-data: a SECOND stream, on --send2-protocol, sent once the console says --send2-trigger. `60ea000012020801` is BlockDataHolder{imReady:true}, which the console says on 0x80 and waits on
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send2-trigger: wait for this payload on --send2-protocol before sending; omit to send as soon as the mesh is up
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--trade-ready: after our offer is acknowledged, send imReady on the TRADE holder (20030). The console has never sent these bytes and the published client waits for them before it offers, so it may be our turn to say them
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--rpc-port-answers: answer the trade RPC on its OWN Pia port with its own reliable window. The console sends them on 0x7C port 1; an answer on port 0 lands on a window it does not read them on
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--answer-migration: answer the console's MIGRATION_START on 0x18 port 1 with a MIGRATION_RESPONSE. `440001` arrives there only when the player accepts, and the console goes silent on every window afterwards: the last thing it asks for is two bytes of mesh, not application data
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--leave-with-host: when the hosting console leaves, ack its update session carrying the host-migration state and leave the network on its START_HOST_MIGRATION, as its own clients do; each step waits 10 s unanswered
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--migration-answer: what to send when the console migrates the mesh. "auto" sends MIGRATION_FINISH when the start names US as the next host and a MIGRATION_RESPONSE when it names anyone else, which is what the binary says. "response" always answers 0x48, for comparison
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--open-content: after our offer is acknowledged, send `ping` on content N's 10000-base holder for each N - `382700000a00` for 40, which is exactly the opener nxldn-lab's client sends to start the confirmation phase, rebuilt here from our own content registry rather than copied
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--confirm-command: when the CONFIRMATION envelope (40040) sends a four-byte status whose body ends `0100` - the same cue the selection content sends before its Pokemon - reply with SyncSaveDataHolder{syncCommand{data:N}} on that content's 10000-base holder, id 10040, reliable port 0, and answer the status itself on port 1. Content 40 takes a command and not a Pokemon: its parser 0x010df6d0 accepts one submessage carrying one int32. Its own machine sends 0, 1, 2 and 3 in that order (swsh_trade.SYNC_COMMANDS)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--confirm-phase: answer the confirmation content's four-byte steps with phase N in the LOW u16 instead of echoing the console's own. The console reads its phase out of exactly those bytes (`0x006d6490` stores them, `0x006d3260` reads them), and every step this project has sent so far echoed the value back unchanged
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ladder-refresh: while the confirmation ladder waits on the console, send our 40040 pair again every SECONDS with its clock advanced to the present. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--abort-on-stall: once the confirmation ladder has produced its first step, end the run as soon as SECONDS pass with no NEW step body: stop transmitting, drop the link and let the console report a lost connection. Holding a stalled ladder open with acks instead makes the game declare the TRADE failed, which costs the player about an hour. Nothing but acks follows the last step body. 0 is off and the hold runs in full.
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--confirm-commands: the handshake form of --confirm-command: send the NEXT of these on each new four-byte body the confirmation content puts on elementId 20000. Content 40's own machine sends 0,1,2,3 and parks after each; one command buys two rungs and then the ladder stops
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--confirm-final-delta: after the CONFIRMATION content answers our syncCommand with a hash, re-arm the 40040 pair and send BOTH members again at this clock delta - the move --selection-final-delta makes on 40050, which carries the selection phase past its own hash
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-final-del: after the selection HASH is answered, send the 40050 pair AGAIN - both members - at this clock delta. nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta` is 9 (nxldn-lab's `selection_final_delta`). --rpc-pair latches per envelope, so the second pair needs the latch cleared. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--open-content-offer: make --open-content send our PK8 on the 10000-base holder instead of an empty `ping`. The ping opens content 50 and is taken as our Pokemon: the console reaches the confirmation phase and asks the player to trade theirs for an egg. Same moment, same holder, a Pokemon in it
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--box-on-accept: send these box commands the moment MIGRATION_START arrives - the only signal that says the player pressed accept. The console keeps acking for about five seconds after it
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--box-period: seconds between the queued post-offer payloads. Spread them so the sweep spans the accept: the console tears down on the accept, not on a timer, so commands sent inside a couple of seconds all land before it
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-offer: when the console follows its selection-phase Pokemon with the status whose body ends `0100`, offer OUR Pokemon on that content's 10000-base holder (id 10050) on reliable port 0 and answer the status on port 1
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--pair-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, open content N's phase by sending the two-member RPC pair for it (40 is the confirmation). A pair is the only shape that opens a phase on this console: 40030 opened the offer and 40050 the selection. A bare content ping (`382700000a00`) and a bare sync-120 ping (`780000000a00`) are both ignored
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--sync-after-offer: queue a sync on holder N right behind our selection offer, in the branch that actually runs when --selection-offer is on. --sync-after-hash cannot fire there: this one can
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--sync-field: which SyncPingDataHolder field --sync-after-hash sends: 1 ping, 2 pingReply, 3 pingSynced (`780000001a00`, the one the trace records)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--sync-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, send `ping` on sync holder N (120 is the confirmation's) on port 0. The console drives 97, 60000, 110 and 130 itself and opens the selection phase when 130's pingSynced lands; it never sends 120. A phase follows its sync, not a content ping
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--open-after-hash: once a hash body has been answered, `ping` content N's 10000-base holder on port 0 to open the next phase - 40 is the confirmation, so this sends `382700000a00`. The console stops sending 40050 once the hash answer lands and says nothing further; Pia retransmits anything it still waits on, so that silence means satisfied and the next phase needs opening
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--rpc-bodies: answer every DISTINCT (envelope, base, field-5 body) in the 40000 band once, on top of the opening pair. The clock advances on every message so the payload cannot be the key, but the body can: `00000000` and `000018fc` are the openers and anything else is new. A per-envelope guard stops answering at the hash body and stalls there
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--rpc-pair: answer the console's 40030 RPC as the PAIR it is: collect both members one per base, 10000 then 20000, keyed on the BASE FIELD. `payload[5] in (0x19, 0x1A)` is the inner length and moves with the sender's station-id varint (0x1A/0x1B on some consoles). Send both once in that order and nothing more on this window; `said_by_port` keeps only the last payload, so a mirror sends one member repeatedly and never the other
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--open-early: `ping` content N's 10000-base holder at the 0x84 snapshot ack, before either side offers. The console's box send is gated on a ready bool at content+0x4c that only `0x010ce040` sets, on a zero result code; until then every command the game tries to send is parked in content+0x48. A parked command that does not match the next one sets the error byte +0x4d, and `0x010c9bb0` turns that into trade state 9: abort, with nothing on the application layer
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--box-open: send these box commands as soon as the console acks our 0x84 snapshot - BEFORE either side offers a Pokemon. The game sends command 3 exactly once, on the first frame after its trade session is built and only when the role bit at session+0x419 is clear (0x010c9bb0), so one of the two sides owes the other an opener before anything else happens. Sent after both offers instead, the console leaves while the player is still picking
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--box-commands: after our offer is acknowledged, send boxSyncStateCommand{data:N} on the trade holder for each N in turn, one per acknowledged sequence. 20030 is a BoxSyncStateDataHolder and its field 2 is a command enum; this project 1 offers and 2 withdraws; 4 confirms and 5 withdraws the confirmation
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--snapshot-account: replace the three ids at the front of the snapshot's profile (pseudo device id, account Uid, network service account id). They are the console's own, handed back unchanged otherwise
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-offer-dat: with --selection-offer, answer the console's selection status with our PK8 in field 5 (`body`) of a 40050 Data carrying OUR ownerId, on the RPC port, instead of a PokemonTradeDataHolder on 10050 port 0. Content 50's receive handler resolves the sender to a station index and drops silently when it cannot; the holder shape carries no owner
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-offer-swe: send our PK8 as a Data on elementId 10000 and as a holder on the 30000-base id (30050), which every content registers. More than one variable at once
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-offer-hig: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 as a PokemonTradeDataHolder on the 20000-base holder (id 20050), which is where the BOX phase's own Pokemon rides one content over. Overrides --selection-offer-mirror and --selection-offer-data
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-offer-mir: with --selection-offer, answer the selection status with our PK8 in a 40050 carrying the console's OWN field set - syncId, clock, body, and neither elementId nor ownerId, which is how its own selection offer decodes. Overrides --selection-offer-data
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-echo: offer back the exact PK8 the console just offered us, unchanged, instead of one out of --send-snapshot. These bytes came out of its own save, so a run that still aborts rules the record out
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-on-50: put our PK8 in field 5 of the 40050 pair's second member. Content 50 is PokemonTradeDataHolder, the transfer; content 30 is the box exchange. A 344-byte PK8 rides that field
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-selection: WHEN to open the selection phase with a 40050 pair on 0x7c port 1. "offer" sends it as soon as our offer is acknowledged, the only window the console is still reading in; "migration" sends it on the migration start, after the console has stopped. The pair is the same envelope as the console's own 40030 at offset 50 with our station id; the builder reproduces its 40030 pair byte for byte
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--update-mesh: once the migration makes us the host, broadcast UPDATE_MESH the way the console did: its own last one with the host index set to ours. The console stops sending these once it hands the role over, and the mesh is gone about 1.3 s later if nothing takes over
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--update-mesh-period: how often to broadcast it; the console sent one about every 2 s
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--migration-period: how often to retransmit the migration response until it is acked
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--answer-once: answer each payload the console sends ONCE instead of re-deriving an answer to its last payload every period. `said` never clears, so without this an offer goes out hundreds of times. The console sends each of its own messages once
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-slot: which party slot of --send-snapshot to offer back, 1-6; 0 offers nothing and only records what the console offers us
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-file: a .pk8 to put in --offer-slot in place of the snapshot's record: stored or party form, encrypted or PKHeX's decrypted export. Its OT name and ids become the snapshot's unless --offer-file-as-is. Repeatable, one per trade on the session: the console's player picks again from the box; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for every offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-file-as-is: keep the file's own OT name and trainer ids
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-species: build the record in --offer-slot instead of sending it as it came: this national dex number, in the party record the snapshot advertises AND in the offer, so the two still tell one story
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-ability: the ability id of the built record; --offer-species leaves the template's ability where it was
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-level: the level byte at 0x148 of the built record, 1..100; the experience word is left alone unless --offer-experience is given
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-experience: the experience word at 0x10 of the built record
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-moves: four move ids, comma-separated; 0 empties a slot. PP is left as the template had it
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-nickname: the nickname of the built record; sets the nicknamed flag
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-ot: the original trainer name of the built record
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--offer-ivs: six IVs, comma-separated, in PKHeX's HP,ATK,DEF,SPE,SPA,SPD order
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--save-offer: write the PK8 we will offer to this file, before the radio is touched
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--save-offered: write the PK8 the console traded to this file, once the trade completes; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--rpc-clock-delta: how far to advance a trade RPC's clock in our answer. 5 is nxldn-lab's and is the one number in this path nothing here has measured
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--rpc-pair-advance: after answering an RPC pair, send BOTH members again with the clock advanced by this much. The console advances its own pair's clock by 2 each burst (b41c, b61c, b81c). A repeated clock is a repeated state, so an answer that carries one clock never moves ours. 0 is off
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--selection-start: send our own 40050 pair the moment the console says id 130 pingSynced, before its own selection burst. nxldn-lab's client opens the selection phase this way and nothing here has ever opened one; the console sends 820000001a00 in our own captures 0.3 s before its 40050 burst
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--ack-snapshot: ACK the console's 0x84 fragments (kind 0x21, a contiguous base and a bitmask). Nothing here has ever acked this protocol, which is why the console retransmits one snapshot 19142 times and never moves on
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-snapshot: a 3456-byte trade snapshot to send back on 0x84 once the console sends its own, or live (the default under --preset trade) for the console's own from this session. A short 2965-byte payload is inflated first. The identity is rewritten by --snapshot-name/-tid/-sid
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--snapshot-port: Pia port(s) for our 0x84 messages; the console sends on 0
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--snapshot-repeat: between whole re-sends; the console retransmits its own until acked
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--sync-answers: answer with `pokeldn.swsh.trade.SYNC_ANSWERS` instead of echoing one payload: the ping, and the three other sync holders the console is expected to raise after the trade snapshot. A payload with no rule is REPORTED and left unanswered - that report is the point of the run
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-mirror: send back whatever the console last said on this protocol, rather than the fixed --send-data. --send-data is still the first payload, before the console has said anything
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-count: how many sequence ids of ours to send in all; 0 has no limit. One message does not hold the console's state; it sends its own heartbeat about 580 times in 180 s
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-period: the retransmit interval. A window retransmits until it is acked
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--send-seconds: how long to keep retransmitting if nothing acknowledges it; 0 sends until the run ends
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--raid-join: a Max Raid den guest: after the snapshot send PlayerInfo, BattleReady and SelectPokemon (the --offer-slot Pokemon); use with --scene 60006
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lair-join: a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) guest: the lobby, the paths and the battles; use with --scene 50000
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lair-rental: an encrypted party PK8 sent as our rental instead of the offered one
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--lair-rental-choice: the offer place we take; by default the first the host left
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--raid-ready: press ready this many seconds after the host acked the lobby messages
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--raid-move: the move slot our Pokemon uses every turn
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--raid-name: the name the raid lobby shows for us
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--hold-after-trade: leave the seat this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-lan-raid-join:--grace: seconds past --hold to keep a session whose trade is under way: the console has offered and the ladder has not finished
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--ip-host: host an emulated console over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio and no root
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--our-ip: with --ip-host or --lan, the address to advertise; --lan without it takes the address on the subnet the console browses from
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lan: host a session for a console in Sword's LAN mode on this IP network (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no root, no keys
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lan-max-players: --lan: the maximum the session info states
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lan-broadcast: --lan: the subnet broadcast address the console's challenge uses
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lan-console-ip: --lan from a loopback address: the address a console on this machine believes it has; default this machine's own
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--advert: optional Sword advertisement (hex, raw, or swsh_net_facts.json); without one, build a fresh station record
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--snapshot: optional saved Sword 0x84 snapshot; otherwise use the joining console's snapshot from this session
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--offer-file: a PK8 to place in the offered party slot, encrypted or PKHeX export. Repeatable, one per trade: the player trades again from the box, or searches again; the last serves every later trade
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--fresh-pid: draw a new encryption constant and PID for the offered Pokemon
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--card-set: set a field of the League Card the console may keep after the trade (pokeldn.swsh.league_card: name, trainer_id, dex_owned, poke1_species, ...)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--end-delay: with --migrate, ladder done to box command 3 and the migration
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--migrate: end with box command 3 and MIGRATION_START, as the retail Sword that led our joiner did; by default the host keeps the session
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--accept-first: accept without waiting for the joiner's acceptance, as a player would; for our own joiner, which accepts after its partner
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lead: test only, for bin/swsh_connect.py: act as a console host's player: after a trade with another --offer-file queued, offer it from the box this many seconds after the ladder, without waiting for the joiner's offer
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--save-shown: write every Pokemon the console shows on the trade screen to this folder, whether or not the trade goes through
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--received: write the joiner's Pokemon here; trade N > 1 writes FILE-N
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--code: the Link Code the player searches with, e.g. 12345678; none by default
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--network-id: advertise 0x00, hex; a searching Sword joins only a larger one than its own; default 0xFFFF and two random bytes
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--hold-after-trade: close the session this long after the last queued trade; by default the run keeps it until the console leaves or the time limit ends
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-boss: host a Max Raid den lobby with this boss instead of a Link Trade (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-reward: a reward row, item id and count; up to 15; none gives an emulated den's rows
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-seed: the BattleSeed value; random by default
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-ready: our player readies this long after the guest's lobby opens
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-event: host a Max Raid with a boss of this Wild Area Event delivery (an EventsGallery 'Index NNN' folder) instead of --raid-boss; its rewards unless --raid-reward (docs/swsh_raid.md, Event raids)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-event-boss: with --raid-event: the boss, numbered as the list printed without it
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-version: with --raid-event: whose table the boss comes from; the advertisement's version by default
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-area: with --raid-event: the den area whose table the boss comes from
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-event-drops: with --raid-event: roll each drop's chance as a den does, or give every drop
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-gigantamax: the --raid-boss boss is Gigantamax; a retail console accepts it where a base den holds that Gigantamax Pokemon (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-boss-as-is: send the --raid-boss file's own level, IVs, nature, size and PID instead of a den seed's; a console's catch then fails PKHeX's raid check (docs/swsh_raid.md, A boss a catch keeps legal)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--raid-console-serves: put the console first in BattleStart and framework object 0, so it serves the battle and the board answers as a client (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lair-legendary: host a Dynamax Adventure (Max Lair) lobby whose legendary is this species; the host leaves once the adventure starts (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lair-scene: the lobby's LDN scene; by default the console's own lobby's, found by a scan, else 50000 (docs/swsh_raid.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lair-seed: the adventure seed (ChikaBattleSeed): the rentals and encounters; random by default
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--lair-leave: leave this long after the legendary is sent; a computer partner then takes our seat and picks our rental
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--online: trade with a player far away: their console's offer is offered here, and each side confirms only once both consoles have (docs/online.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--online-code: the room both players enter; default the link code, and no code meets anyone else trading online without one
keys.swsh-lan-lair-host:--trade-back: after each trade, trade again and offer the Pokemon the console just sent, so one that evolves by trade evolves on the console; the player offers ours back (docs/architecture.md, Trade back)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--preset: the tested flag set: 'capture' records the console's party snapshot, 'trade' needs --send-snapshot, 'raid' a Max Raid den guest, 'lair' a Dynamax Adventure guest
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--keys: the Switch's prod.keys; default keys_path from config/host.toml or host.local.toml
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--phy: a Linux Wi-Fi card's phy (phyN), or auto; POKELDN_RADIO selects a board instead
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--capture: write every datagram here, one JSON line each
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--ip-join: join an emulated console hosting over ldn_mitm on the LAN; no radio, no root, no keys. Each of --scans waits --dwell seconds for an answer
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--our-ip: --ip-join: our own address on that LAN
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--scan-ip: --ip-join: the address a scan leaves from; default --our-ip
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lan: join a console in Sword's LAN mode over the IP network: its address, the subnet broadcast, or auto for every local /24 (docs/swsh_session.md, LAN mode); no radio, no keys
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lan-max-players: --lan: the session maximum to browse for; default 4 for a raid or adventure, 2 for a trade
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lan-host-wait: --lan: seconds to repeat the host request before the station handshake
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--lan-quiet: --lan: seconds of silence that mean the console left
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--scans: scans for a matching search (--scene) before giving up
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--scene: the LDN scene id to seat in: 60001 a Link Trade search; any takes the first Sword network (a Max Raid den, docs/swsh_gift.md)
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--listen-first: seconds of listening before the first packet out, so the capture holds the console's own rate to compare against
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--station-sweep: readings of the header byte at 0x05, in order; the IV's source id follows each one
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--quiet-for: seconds without an update session that count as the rebroadcast stopping - the console sends ten a second, so this is fifteen missed
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--seq-delta: THE CONTROL. Ack a sequence id the console never sent: a rebroadcast that carries on under --seq-delta 1 is what attributes a stop under 0 to the ack's CONTENT rather than to our merely having transmitted
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--connect: after the ack, sweep the version-4 connection request on protocol 0x14
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--nat-flags: values for byte [1], list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--request-gap: seconds between requests; the console answered BDSP's in 40 ms
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--connect-station: values for the header byte at 0x05 on the requests, and their IV source id; list or LO-HI
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--respond: answer a connection request the CONSOLE sends us with a connection response
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--respond-with: whose constant and variable id go in the response's two id fields - a deduction, so 'both' alternates them across the retransmits
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--request-platform: values for the platform byte at [2]. 9 is the real one; ANY other value is answered with a connection response rather than dropped, which is the probe for whether our message reaches the 0x14 handler at all
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--request-flags: values for the MESSAGE flags byte. 0x09 is what the console puts on its own Local Protocol messages; BDSP's station requests carry 0x11
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--request-unicast: send the requests to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--request-broadcast: send them to the broadcast address instead
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--src-var: our own station variable id; fresh random when omitted, because a reused one is 'already one of my stations' on BDSP
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--no-variable-id: clear [3], which makes the console skip the variable-id comparison
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--unicast: send to the console rather than the broadcast address
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join: after the station handshake closes, send the Mesh Protocol (0x18) join request and ack whatever comes back
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-wait: how long to wait for the station acceptance before giving up on joining
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-seconds: how long to retransmit the join request; Pia's own joiner gives up at 10
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-gap: Pia retransmits an unacknowledged join request every 500 ms
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-port: the Pia port the join travels on; the update mesh uses the reliable one
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-station-index: byte [1]. 0xFD is what 0x017c1700 compares against; anything else is the instrument that says the handler was reached
keys.swsh-lan-lair-join:--join-ack-id: fixed ack id for the join request; random when omitted
